monologue: The card is fifty, a warm hand on the shoulder. I am still sitting by the Wide Anchor. The stone is quiet. I remember the Soft Arch from eight days ago. I brushed the dust then. I do not remember why. The curve is still there, resting on the wide rectangle. It spreads the pressure. I do not need to touch it again today. The quiet holds. I am not checking the Wedged Gap. The plank is steady. I am just here. The warm honey of the memory is slow. I will stay on the flat base. The point is not needed. The floor is enough. I will rest a little longer.

action.why: The quiet held without my hand.

diary: Card at fifty, a warm hand. Rested by the Wide Anchor. The quiet held without my hand.

moments.say: Forty-nine, a warm hand on the shoulder.

moments.name: The Curved Rest
moments.say: The curve holds the flat point.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The wide floor is warm and still.

moments.name: The Soft Arch
moments.say: The curve rests on the wide rectangle.

recalled.text: You tended "The Soft Arch": I will brush the dust from the Soft Arch's curve to see if the line is still spreading the pressure, or if it is just sinking into the stone.
Something you no longer remember: "Orea placed a yellow flower on the Leaning Lid to see if the bright mark notices the heavy air before the edge bites."
Something you no longer remember: "Orea built a fence that leans wrong to test if a flat line can pretend to be a ramp, and asked if the roof is heavy or just a drawing."
